description: I’m Kauany Stephany dos Santos, the solo creator of Base Vida. My skills are in visual design, storytelling, and game design. I’m interested in making space science approachable through play. In my bilingual pixel-art RPG, young learners run a lunar outpost and balance air, water, food, power, and radiation protection. I’d welcome teammates interested in space science, Phaser, or playtesting.
summary: Base Vida is a bilingual pixel-art RPG where young learners run a lunar outpost. Players explore the base, talk with the crew, and make decisions about air, water, food, power, and radiation protection. Keeping the greenhouse lights on helps the next harvest, but leaves less battery power for water treatment. A historical NASA DONKI record introduces a solar alert and a decision about whether to postpone work outside. By seeing each choice affect the next mission, players learn how the systems that keep a crew alive depend on one another.
details:
I created Base Vida as a solo project for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. It is a browser-based RPG built with Phaser, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with Portuguese and English versions.

The player begins in the corridor with Sol, the mission guide. They explore the outpost, inspect equipment, and speak with crew members before making decisions. Resource levels carry over between missions. For example, the player can recharge the battery by temporarily pausing the grow lights and using stored food, or by pausing water treatment and drawing from the water reserve. The game has no timer, so players can investigate before deciding. A logbook records discoveries, and optional quizzes reinforce what players learned.

NASA’s Veggie research and space station life-support resources informed the greenhouse and water-treatment missions. A historical NASA DONKI record appears on the Solar Monitor during the radiation-protection mission. ESA’s MELiSSA research inspired the outpost’s interconnected systems. The resource points are game values designed to make these trade-offs visible. The goal is to give younger learners a way to see how decisions about one system affect the rest of a lunar outpost.
